correctness.rationale: Direct proof: the proposed point is feasible with tail mass one. For every feasible y, the residual inner product is bounded by −d(j−1)+e and is attained by the proposed projection; strict convexity proves uniqueness. Its squared norm gives every shell. Both summands rise strictly with omitted-tail count. Strict Jensen/variance identity with distinct residual vectors proves that the continuous farthest points are exactly the specified vertices. Hypergeometric sampling has the stated mean and variance, and its finite-population CLT plus the delta method give the claimed Gaussian limit. The standalone exact checker verifies 168,870 supporting inequalities for 56 small configurations and separate constrained QPs; the proof, not enumeration, covers all admissible parameters.

value.rationale: The panhandle polytope is a canonical one-facet truncation of a hypersimplex arising in matroid relaxation, rather than an ad hoc coordinate slice. The theorem completely quantifies lost Euclidean geometry at all ambient vertices, determines exactly which continuous points are farthest, and identifies the product-of-hypersimplices contact faces. Hypergeometric fluctuations quantify the nontrivial gap between typical and worst-case squared metric errors. A natural family-wide invariant and its asymptotic law are supplied, not a small numerical increment.
